Hi, I'm Yash Pradip Pakale — skilled in coding, data analytics, design/audio, and storytelling.
Building The Earth Information Jukebox: turning NASA's Earth data into sound.
Looking for teammates in:
Backend/data (Python, APIs)
Frontend/UI
Audio/sound design

Let's build something that stands out on demo day!
summary:
TerraVoxis is a web jukebox that lets people listen to NASA Earth visualizations. It was built for the Earth Information Jukebox challenge, with blind and low-vision listeners in mind first.

Most sonification tools turn colour straight into sound. TerraVoxis reads each visualization's colour legend first. It converts every sampled pixel into an estimated data value, such as sea surface temperature, aerosol type or lightning activity. Then it maps that value to pitch, loudness, stereo position and timbre while the NASA animation plays. Listeners can place listening probes with a mouse or the keyboard, learn the mapping from a ten-second audio legend, and choose Scientific, Musical or Accessibility mode. They can also export the soundtrack as a WAV file with a JSON file that documents the mapping.

Every value is labelled "estimated from pixel colour" and shown with a confidence level, so the sound stays honest about its source. TerraVoxis runs entirely in the browser. It has no backend, no accounts and no AI at run time, and it is free. This makes NASA's Earth science stories something you can hear, not only see.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

TerraVoxis turns NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) animations into sound that follows the data. You pick a scene from the jukebox and press play. You then hear the planet: warm currents give high pitches and cold water gives low ones, lightning crackles at the position where each flash appears, and different aerosol types each have their own timbre.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Offline pipeline (Python): downloads the NASA SVS visualizations through the SVS API, transcodes them for the web, and builds a colour-to-value lookup table from each visualization's own legend.

2. In-browser analysis: samples video frames in real time (requestVideoFrameCallback) and converts each pixel colour into an estimated value with the lookup table. It then smooths the values and detects events such as new lightning flashes.

3. Mapping: turns values and events into pitch, loudness, stereo pan and timbre. Pitch follows the data value, not the hue.

4. Audio: the Web Audio API renders the sound live. OfflineAudioContext renders it again for WAV export.

SCENES

- Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature (NASA SVS 3912)

- Lightning from the ISS, 2017–2023 (NASA SVS 5011)

- GEOS Aerosols 2025 (NASA SVS 5669)

KEY FEATURES

- Legend-aware sonification: colour becomes a value before it becomes sound.

- Listening probes: place up to two probes with mouse or keyboard to hear and read the value at that point.

- Audio legend: learn the value-to-sound mapping in about ten seconds before playback.

- Three modes: Scientific (continuous, precise), Musical (pitch snapped to a scale, with reverb), and Accessibility (8 distinct steps, a reference tone, and probes heard one at a time).

- "Describe this moment": a spoken or screen-reader summary of what is on screen.

- Keyboard-first design that works with screen readers. Opt-in vibration cues on Android.

- WAV export plus a JSON file that documents the mapping, for reproducibility.

- Honest provenance: every value is labelled "estimated from pixel colour" and shown with a confidence level.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Most NASA Earth visualizations can only be understood by looking at them. TerraVoxis opens them to blind and low-vision people, and gives sighted users a second way to notice patterns such as the Gulf Stream cooling from about 23 °C near Florida to about 3 °C south of Greenland. Teachers, museums and science communicators can use it with no installation, no account and no cost.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

TypeScript, React 19, React Router 7, Zustand, Tailwind CSS 4, Vite, Web Audio API, Python 3.12 (requests, NumPy, Pillow, imageio-ffmpeg/FFmpeg), Vitest, Playwright, axe-core, oxlint, GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages. The app has no backend and runs entirely in the browser.

WHAT IS CREATIVE ABOUT IT

Most image sonifiers map hue or brightness directly to sound. TerraVoxis reverses each scientific colour map first, so the sound tracks the underlying quantity. It combines research-based auditory design (pitch polarity, auditory legends and reference tones, from published sonification studies) with a playful jukebox interface.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Accessibility first: we tested keyboard-only use and screen-reader announcements, and ran automated axe accessibility checks in Chromium and Firefox through CI.

- Scientific honesty: values are labelled as estimates and not measurements, confidence is shown, and the full method is documented in docs/METHODOLOGY.md.

- Zero cost and privacy: the app has no servers, accounts or tracking.

- Respect for NASA guidelines: the app uses no NASA logos, credits every SVS visualization and its creators, and states that it is not affiliated with NASA.

Live app: https://yash151005.github.io/TerraVoxis/

Source code: https://github.com/Yash151005/TerraVoxis
